name: M01 findCellOptionLines: the memo is rebuilt on every call
why: the parent's cost under another spelling: every call flat-maps every cell again; killed by the identity rows (fresh element objects on a repeat call) and by the clock row (three calls over one lookup: thousands)

name: M02 findCellOptionLines: the cached array itself is returned
why: a caller that reorders or empties its answer corrupts the cache: killed by the different-array row and the mutation row (push, pop, reverse, sort, splice, truncate)

name: M03 findCellOptionLines: the copy leaves out the first element
why: the first option line of every document is missing: killed by every answer row

name: M04 findCellOptionLines: the copy leaves out the last element
why: the last option line is missing: killed by the answer rows (the old-spelling oracle on named and seeded documents)

name: M05 findCellOptionLines: the memo is kept with ||= instead of ??=
why: EQUIVALENT: the field is undefined or an array, and an array (an empty one too) is truthy, so ||= and ??= assign in exactly the same cases

name: M06 findCellOptionLines: the per-cell reader is passed to flatMap bare
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer: flatMap hands the reader (cell, index, array), and cellOptionLinesOf declares one parameter, so the extra arguments are ignored; the laziness row counts REFERENCES to cellOptionLinesOf (a call and a bare one alike), so the spelling is not a kill either (an earlier row that counted calls only killed it by its spelling: fixed)

name: M07 findCellOptionLines: the first cell is skipped
why: the first cell's option lines are missing: killed by the answer rows

name: M08 findCellOptionLines: only the first cell is read
why: every cell but the first is missing: killed by the answer rows and the 2,000-cell premise of the clock row

name: M09 scanEntry: the option lines are built eagerly with the scan
from: const entry: RegionsCacheEntry = { text, engine, mode, regions: computeRegions(text, engine, mode) };
to:
const scanned = computeRegions(text, engine, mode);
  const entry: RegionsCacheEntry = { text, engine, mode, regions: scanned, optionLines: scanned.cells.flatMap((cell) => cellOptionLinesOf(cell)) };
why: every surface that scans (the Outline, the tint, Run Cell, cross-references) pays for the option lines it never asks for: the answers are the same, so only the laziness row sees it (the callers of cellOptionLinesOf in the model are findCellOptionLines and scanEntry, not findCellOptionLines alone)

name: M10 scanEntry: a cache hit forgets the option lines
from:
if (hitAt !== 0) regionsCache = promoted(regionsCache, hitAt);
    return hit;
why: any lookup of the scan (findAllCells, inFrontMatter, buildOutline) drops the memo: the next findCellOptionLines flat-maps again; killed by the row that asks findAllCells between two calls (fresh elements) and the clock row's lookups

name: M11 scanEntry: the memo is dropped when a hit is not at the front
from:
if (hitAt !== 0) regionsCache = promoted(regionsCache, hitAt);
    return hit;
to:
if (hitAt !== 0) { hit.optionLines = undefined; regionsCache = promoted(regionsCache, hitAt); }
    return hit;
why: the blind list is rebuilt whenever the engine-aware scan was asked in between (the two keys of one document alternate in an edit cycle): killed by the row that asks the blind and the aware lists in turn and expects the blind elements back

name: T01 clock row: the ratio limit is 1e12
why: a recorded gap of the clock row on its own: with no limit the row still ticks its windows, and the identity rows are the witness of the memo (M01 is killed by them); the limit's value is held by its figure in the header (the parent 15,000, the cure under 10)

name: T02 clock row: the ratio limit is 3 (under the cure's own figure)
why: three copies of 4,000 elements over a copy of 2,000 cells are 6 to 9 lookups: a limit under that fails the cure, so the row is live and measures what it says

name: T03 seeded row: the floor on documents with an option line is 399
why: not every one of the 400 documents holds an option line: the floor fails when raised to all of them, so the draw's floor of 200 is a real count and not a constant that cannot fail

name: T04 seeded row: the floor on documents whose lists differ by engine is 399
why: most documents agree under every engine; the floor of 20 is a real count of the documents where a wrong key would show

name: H01 ratioOfWindows: the baseline window reads the work window's end
why: a clock stuck in the baseline window (Learning 910): the ratio is 1/0, the smallest window 0, and the clock row fails as 'did not tick'; killed by the helper's own rows and the clock row, which pass at the cure without the edit

name: H02 ratioOfWindows: the baseline window is not among the smallest
from: smallest = Math.min(smallest, t1 - t0, t2 - t1);
why: a baseline window that did not tick is not noticed: killed by the helper row whose baseline reads 0

name: H03 ratioOfWindows: the work window is not among the smallest
from: smallest = Math.min(smallest, t1 - t0, t2 - t1);
why: a work window that did not tick is not noticed: killed by the helper row whose work reads 0 (the stuck clock) and the spin row

name: H04 ratioOfWindows: the largest round decides, not the median
why: one pause in a work window decides the row: killed by the helper row with a pause in the work window of the middle round (500 against 5)

name: H05 ratioOfWindows: the smallest round decides, not the median
why: one pause in a baseline window decides the row: killed by the helper row with a pause in the baseline window of the middle round (0.1 against 5)

name: H06 ratioOfWindows: the ratio is not normalised by the repeats of the work
why: a window of 4 repeats against a window of 8 repeats is not one unit against one unit: killed by the helper row with 4 and 8 repeats (exactly 20)

name: H07 ratioOfWindows: the ratio is not normalised by the repeats of the baseline
why: killed by the helper row with 4 and 8 repeats (exactly 20)

name: H08 clockBreaks: a ratio that is not a number is accepted
why: EQUIVALENT in the count of breaks: a NaN ratio fails `run.ratio < ratioLimit` and so does an Infinity one, so without the line the same single break is reported with the generic message instead of 'the ratio is ...'; no row reads the message of that break (the line exists to name the cause)
